clue.text: Flower of 21 somewhat given to flirting

definitions.meaning: a flower here is something that flows, a river
the old adjective means flirtatious, coy and teasing in manner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword favourite for a river (a thing that flows); 21 across is NORTHUMBERLAND, the English county where this river reaches the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coquet is a Northumberland river, and as an adjective the word is an old form of coquettish, inclined to flirt.

clue.text: Cents and shillings have forerunners

indicators.note: the runners at the front of each of these four words, their opening letters, are what is wanted

explanation.surface: A remark that pennies and shillings had predecessors in the history of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have forerunners' tells you to take the first letters of Cents, and, shillings, have; the whole clue also describes money in coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins such as cents and shillings are ready money, so the clue describes it as a whole.

clue.text: Girl largely reticent, even contained

indicators.note: contained says the shortened word holds the next piece within it
largely means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: reticent means quiet, saying little
e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: A girl described as mostly reserved and even-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the last letter of the reticent word and 'contained' puts the poetic form of even inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Queenie is a girl's pet name, once a common English given name.

clue.text: Far from reticent one in business interrupting departure

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the word for departure

parts.note: a departure is an exit

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the business abbreviation

parts.note: PLC, public limited company, is a British type of business
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone outspoken who barges into a company meeting just as people are leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'interrupting' nest the pieces: one inside the business, and that inside the departure. PLC (public limited company) is the British counterpart of a listed corporation.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit means stated plainly and openly, the opposite of being reserved or reticent.

clue.text: 21's version of the human lot

indicators.note: a version is a reworking, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A remark about how a county sees the human condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link word; 'version of' rearranges HUMAN LOT. '21's' means a place belonging to NORTHUMBERLAND (21 across).
explanation.definitionFit: Alnmouth is a coastal village in Northumberland, so it is that county's own place.

clue.text: 21's line in underworld, a long way to its region

parts.note: taken as written
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for the underworld itself
a long way means far
NE, the north-east, is the region of England where Northumberland lies

explanation.surface: A line drawn in the underworld, stretching a long way to its outer region.
explanation.walkthrough: '21's' means a place belonging to NORTHUMBERLAND (21 across); 'its region' is that county's region, the north-east of England, NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lindisfarne, Holy Island, lies off the Northumberland coast and belongs to the county.

clue.text: Hardly able to see setter's film about love

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so his own is MY
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
pic is short for a picture, a film

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler's romantic movie is something you can barely watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the film round the love letter; love means nil in tennis scoring, hence the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sighted people struggle to see distant things clearly, which is what myopic describes.

clue.text: Loth to remove party from reactor site and insert number

indicators.note: insert tells you to put the number into what remains
remove says the party word comes out of the place name

parts.note: Dounreay, on the north coast of Scotland, was the site of a nuclear reactor
a do is a party
D is 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Reluctant to strip festivities from a nuclear plant and add another figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove party from' takes DO out of DOUNREAY, leaving UNREAY; 'insert number' adds D (Roman 500) to give UNREA(D)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Unready means unwilling or not prepared, close to being loth or reluctant to act.

clue.text: Prevented accepting name for buttocks

indicators.note: accepting means the word for prevented takes the next piece inside

parts.note: to be hindered is to be held back or prevented

explanation.surface: Someone who was stopped from taking a name for their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts N inside HINDERED: HINDER(N)ED, then split 6-3.
explanation.definitionFit: The hind end is a jocular term for the rump or backside.

clue.text: Agent holding general is likely to go off

indicators.note: holding means the agent word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A secret agent has a general in custody who might explode at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' suggests a bomb or bad food; here it means drop off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drowsy is likely to nod off or go off to sleep soon.

clue.text: Fled with gold before coming from the Pyrenees?

indicators.note: before places the gold piece ahead of the word for fled

parts.note: with means and, joining things
or is gold in heraldry
fled means ran away

explanation.surface: A fugitive who ran off with gold before arriving from the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: Andorra is just one country in the Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: An Andorran comes from Andorra, a small country set high in the Pyrenees mountains.

clue.text: Present record speed's about one a minute, which is wild

parts.note: present, as in at home, is in
a record is a disc

indicators.note: about means the speed word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: speed is rate; the 's stands for has
one is I, the Roman numeral
MIN is the standard abbreviation for a minute

explanation.surface: A gift recorded at a wild pace, one a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the speed round one and a minute. 'which is' is a link, and 'Present' means here, at hand, rather than a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiscriminate means random and unrestrained, as wild shots or wild accusations are.

clue.text: Copper alloy in negative encountered in waterway

indicators.note: in places the negative and the meeting word inside the waterway

parts.note: a canal is a man-made waterway
non is a negative prefix
encountered means met

explanation.surface: A metal alloy described in the negative, met with along a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the negative and the encounter inside the waterway; the answer is then split 6-5.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannon metal, also called gun metal, is a bronze alloy of copper and tin once used for guns.

clue.text: Indicate future setting of gins, if in quarry

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters within the quarry word

parts.note: a hunter's quarry is its prey, the animal pursued

indicators.note: a setting is an arrangement, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Predicting what will come after setting gin traps in a quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting of' rearranges only 'gins'; 'if' follows it unchanged, and 'in' puts both inside the prey. Gin traps suit the hunting picture of the quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: To presignify is to foreshadow, signalling something before it happens.

clue.text: Rich, turning up, is on cue

indicators.note: turning means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone getting richer, arriving exactly on cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' looks like arriving, but 'turning' rearranges UP IS ON CUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecunious means well supplied with money, wealthy, the opposite of impecunious.

clue.text: Flower of 21 and of 20, nearly

annotationWithheld.why: Flower of 21 and of 20, nearly: TYNE is hidden in 'twenTY NEarly' with the numeral 20 read as the word twenty, which the hidden-word check cannot read from the printed digits

clue.text: Confused premier accepting measure for measure

indicators.note: accepting means the premier's letters take the measure inside

parts.note: PM, prime minister, is the premier
an ell is an old measure of cloth length
a second ell, the same old cloth measure

explanation.surface: A muddled prime minister trading one measure for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts one measure inside the premier, and the second follows; 'for' is a link. The ell was an old English cloth length of about 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: Pell-mell means in a confused, disorderly rush.

clue.text: Set of teeth for honey

definitions.meaning: a hair-grooming tool is a row of teeth
bees store honey in a waxy structure of cells, the honeycomb

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as a cell structure used for honey, as in honeycomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A comb is both a toothed grooming tool and the wax cell structure bees build to hold honey.

clue.text: 21's right to enter doth despond

indicators.note: to enter says the right letter goes into the next word

parts.note: doth despond is old-fashioned for is gloomy, which is mopeth, archaic for mopes

explanation.surface: A dejected figure, in old-fashioned language, with the right to come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts right inside the old -eth verb form for mopes. '21's' means a town of the county at 21 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Morpeth is the county town of Northumberland.

clue.text: Confused about rule breaking being good in "Animal Farm"

indicators.note: about means the confused word goes round the next piece

parts.note: to be fogged is to be confused or befuddled

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of the word are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Muddled about broken rules in Orwell's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges rule and 'about' puts the result inside the confused word. In Orwell's Animal Farm the animals chant "Four legs good, two legs bad".
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's fable the slogan declares that animals on all fours are good, two-legged humans bad.

clue.text: 0s coming out from 12?

parts.note: the round 0 shapes are balls fired from a cannon, 12 down being CANNON METAL

explanation.walkthrough: 12 down is CANNON METAL; the 0s are round balls fired from a cannon, a kind of gun. The blogger was unsure of the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Round balls fired out of a cannon are shot from a gun, a cryptic picture of that ammunition.

clue.text: Common sense started and ran

indicators.note: started means only the start, the first letter, of sense

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, so ran is hared

explanation.surface: Common sense got going and then took off running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common sense' reads as one phrase, but 'Common' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in common is shared between several people.

clue.text: Nanny trainer accepts hitchhiker called Percy

indicators.note: accepts means the nanny college takes the next piece inside

parts.note: Norland College in Bath is a famous British college that trains nannies
a hitchhiker thumbs lifts, so is a thumber

explanation.surface: A nanny's tutor takes in a hitchhiker named Percy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts the hitchhiker inside the nanny college. The Percy family hold the dukedom of this county, and the duke is called by its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Percy family hold the title Earl or Duke of Northumberland and are called by it.

clue.text: Address to people that seems to 13 across

parts.note: O is the vocative word used in addressing someone, as in O king
people can be men

explanation.surface: A speech to the people that seems to predict the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O men!' is a speech opening; 13 across is PRESIGNIFY, so the definition is a thing that seems to foretell the future.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign that seems to foretell what is going to happen.

clue.text: Exaggerate measure of advantage to spinners

definitions.meaning: to exaggerate a thing's worth is to think it better than it is
in cricket the ... counts overs bowled per hour, and spin bowlers, with short run-ups, keep it high

explanation.walkthrough: Spinners are slow bowlers in cricket, who get through their overs quickly, which helps a team's over rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrate is to value too highly; the cricket term is a rate of overs, which spin bowlers boost.

clue.text: Spell "meat" in 21

parts.note: a hex is a spell or curse
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A recipe direction to spell out the meat in a county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 21' defines a place in NORTHUMBERLAND (21 across).
explanation.definitionFit: Hexham is a market town in Northumberland, on the Tyne.

clue.text: Abandon Christmas, say, according to plan

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken and sound like another

parts.note: to abandon is to shed, and Christmas is Yule

explanation.surface: Cancelling Christmas as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the answer sounds like 'shed Yule'. 'according to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable or programme, a plan of what happens when.

clue.text: On 21's border — about time too — to follow its leader

indicators.note: to follow puts the leader letter after the rest
about means the word for too goes round the time letter

parts.note: too means also
its refers to 21 across, NORTHUMBERLAND, whose leading letter is N

explanation.surface: Something on the county boundary, also late, trailing behind its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: ALSO round T gives ALSTO, and N follows. Alston is in fact just over the border in Cumbria, which the Guardian later corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: Alston is a town in Cumbria close to the Northumberland boundary, so it lies on the county's border.
